extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners; USPTO examiners and administrative patent judges
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for taking an appeal from a patent examiner to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (and further appellate/court review), including notice, brief content, timing, fees, remands, and post-decision handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal / Notice of Appeal eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 37 CFR 1.191 an applicant whose claims have been twice or finally rejected may appeal; a patent owner may appeal adverse ex parte reexamination decisions; a third-party requester in an inter partes proceeding may appeal only in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be taken by filing a notice of appeal and paying the required fee within the time periods provided by 37 CFR 1.134 and 1.136. A notice of appeal may be filed after any claim has been twice rejected, even if not finally rejected. Different rules apply for reexaminations depending on the filing date of the original application; appeals in inter partes reexamination are governed by separate sections (37 CFR 1.959–1.981).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fees and fee payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are required for filing an appeal, filing the brief in support of the appeal, and requesting an oral hearing (see 35 U.S.C. 41 and 37 CFR 1.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal fee must accompany the notice of appeal (or be paid within the time for reply if petitioned). A fee under 37 CFR 1.17(c) is required when the brief is filed. If a notice of appeal includes an unsigned authorization to charge fees, the notice may be unacceptable. (MPEP lists numeric fees current as of the manual's date.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing the appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.192(a) requires the appellant to file a brief in triplicate within two months from the date of the notice of appeal or within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken, if later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the brief with the requisite fee within the time allowed results in dismissal of the appeal. Time periods may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (up to five months ordinarily) or 1.136(b) (extraordinary circumstances). Special rules apply in reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.550(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s brief must be filed in triplicate and include fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be filed in triplicate and be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three copies of the brief are required so the Board and examiner can be provided with the positions and any relied-upon references. If appellant relies on a reference, three copies of that reference should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — real party in interest (37 CFR 1.192(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying the real party in interest, if the party named in the caption is not the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows Board members to comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules. If not named, the examiner will assume the captioned party is the real party in interest, but the Board may require explicit naming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — related appeals and interferences (37 CFR 1.192(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by number and filing date all other appeals or interferences known to appellant (or counsel/assignee) that will directly affect or be affected by the Board's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List appeal/interference numbers and filing dates. If none are identified, the examiner will presume there are none; the Board may require explicit identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — status of claims (37 CFR 1.192(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of all claims (pending, cancelled, allowed, rejected, etc.) and identification of the claims on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids confusion as to which claims are on appeal and their precise wording, especially if amendments were made after final rejection. Each appealed claim must be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — status of amendments (37 CFR 1.192(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of any amendment filed subsequent to final rejection and whether it was entered, denied entry, or entered in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State status as understood by the appellant so disagreements about post-final amendments can be resolved before Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — summary of the invention (37 CFR 1.192(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the invention defined in the claims involved in the appeal, referring to the specification by page and line and to drawings by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably 'read' the appealed claims on the specification and drawings; page/line references help the Board quickly locate claimed subject matter in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — issues (37 CFR 1.192(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of the issues presented for review, each corresponding to a separate ground of rejection appellant wishes the Board to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue should include its basis (e.g., 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones'). The statement should be concise but not omit the basis of each issue, and should not include argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — grouping of claims (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection that applies to a group of two or more claims, the Board will select a single claim from the group and decide the appeal on that claim alone unless appellant includes a statement that the claims do not stand or fall together and explains why they are separately patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely pointing out differences among claims is insufficient; appellant must explain why claims are separately patentable in the appropriate part of the argument. Failure to assert separate patentability is treated as concession that the ground applies equally to all grouped claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the appeal brief — argument requirements (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must set forth appellant’s contentions with respect to each issue and the basis therefor, with citations to authorities, statutes, and parts of the record. Each issue should be treated under a separate heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any argument or authority not included in the brief will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown. Oral argument will not cure defects of a brief; the Board expects a full statement of positions so no record search is necessary to understand appellant's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument specifics for 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the argument must specify the errors in the rejection and how the first paragraph of 112 is complied with, including how the specification and drawings describe the subject matter, enable one skilled in the art to make and use it, and set forth the best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite pages/lines of the specification and drawings as appropriate; explain how each of the statutory requirements is satisfied for the rejected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument specifics for 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the argument shall specify the errors in the rejection and how the claims particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain claim language and why it meets the definiteness requirement; point out errors in examiner’s claim interpretation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument specifics for 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the argument must specify the errors in the rejection and why the rejected claims are patentable under 102, including any specific claim limitations not described in the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific limitations absent from the cited reference; a general statement that not all limitations are in a single reference is insufficient without pointing out which limitations are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument specifics for 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the argument shall specify the errors and, where appropriate, identify claim limitations not described in the applied prior art and explain how such limitations render the claimed subject matter unobvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection is based on a combination of references, explain why the references, taken as a whole, do not suggest the claimed subject matter and, if appropriate, why features disclosed in one reference may not properly be combined with features disclosed in another. Mere assertion that limitations aren't in a single reference is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument specifics for other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections other than 112/102/103, the argument must specify errors in the rejection and the specific limitations or reasons why the rejection is in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the argument to the statutory or rule-based rejection at issue and identify record support for appellant's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be included with the brief (37 CFR 1.192(c)(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exact claim wording to avoid confusion as to the claims on appeal; aids the Board and examiner in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliance notification and one-month amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with 37 CFR 1.192(c), the appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and given one month to file an amended brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant fails to file an amended brief within one month, or the amended brief does not overcome the stated reasons, the appeal will stand dismissed. The examiner may use specified form paragraphs to notify the appellant of deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se appellant brief exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If the brief is filed by an appellant who is not represented by a registered practitioner and the brief was neither prepared nor signed by a registered practitioner, the brief need only substantially comply with items (1), (2), and (8) of 37 CFR 1.192(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, it will be presumed that claims of a rejected group stand or fall together unless the pro se appellant provides reasons why certain claims are separately patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed during brief period
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment presented within the period for filing the brief places the application in condition for allowance, the amendment may be entered; amendments should not be included in the appeal brief but filed as separate papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1207 and §§ 1215.01–1215.02 for handling. An amendment entered during the brief period preserves pending status for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to file brief or defective notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the brief (or failure to pay required fees) within the time allowed results in dismissal of the appeal and may result in abandonment of the application unless claims stand allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claims stand allowed, dismissal does not cause abandonment and the application is returned to the examiner for action on allowed claims. In reexamination proceedings, failure to file a brief leads to issuance of the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to file the brief (37 CFR 1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant who cannot file the brief within the time allotted may petition the Technology Center for additional time under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Additional time in excess of five months will not be granted except for extraordinary circumstances under 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the notice of appeal, appeal fee, petition under 1.136(a), and petition fee are filed will be the date of the reply and used to determine the extension period and fee amounts. Time extended is added to the original calendar day of the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters handled concurrently with appeal — reasons notice may be unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs identify typical defects in a notice of appeal, including unpaid fee, no second rejection, untimely filing, or claims allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee unpaid, applicant may obtain an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but cannot reply later than the maximum six-month statutory period (and cannot get more than five months additional without extraordinary circumstances). If claims were allowed or no second rejection, the notice is unacceptable and will be returned with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant must address every ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant's brief must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner; failure to address any ground will lead to notification to correct the brief and may not be cured by oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if appellant considers a ground 'clearly improper', reasons must be given to the Board explaining that belief. The mere filing of paper titled 'brief' does not guarantee compliance; the brief must set forth authorities and arguments relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide copies of referenced materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant relies on some reference in the brief, appellant is expected to provide the Board with three copies of that reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying copies helps the Board and examiner consider the reference without needing to search external records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling and docketing of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte appeals and related papers are forwarded to the Technology Center (TC) for docketing and processing. Memorandum PTO-262 is attached to the file wrapper when remanded by the Board to keep records current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TC must promptly complete and forward memorandum PTO-262 when the application is allowed, prosecution is reopened, a continuation is filed, or appeal discontinued. Applications once made 'special' remain special during appeal if diligent prosecution is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/31 for Notice of Appeal recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a separate letter containing the notice of appeal is strongly recommended; Form PTO/SB/31 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate, properly prepared notice reduces processing delays associated with defective notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against entry of new ground of rejection in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The heading (and MPEP practice) indicates that examiners are generally prohibited from entering a new ground of rejection for the first time in the Examiner’s Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where new grounds are proposed, the Board or examiner must follow prescribed procedures (e.g., Board may treat as new ground and give appellant opportunity to respond or remand). Specifics are set out in MPEP sections dealing with Examiner’s Answer and New Grounds by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by the Board (consideration of amendments, affidavits/declarations, or further search)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand the application to the examiner to consider amendments, affidavits/declarations, or for further search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remands may be used when the Board needs the examiner to consider newly presented matter or perform further searching; procedures and form PTO-262 usage apply on remand to keep the file current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing requests (fee and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may request an oral hearing before the Board; a fee is required (see 35 U.S.C. 41/37 CFR 1.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for oral hearing must accompany the filing and fee; oral argument will not cure a defective brief that fails to address grounds of rejection. The Office processes oral hearing requests according to Board rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Federal Circuit — notice and filing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When appealing to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, the appellant must file in the Patent Office a written notice of appeal directed to the Director within the time prescribed (at least 60 days) and must file a copy with the Clerk of the Federal Circuit and pay the docket fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.302 describes methods (mail to Box 8, Express Mail per 37 CFR 1.10, or hand delivery to Office of the Solicitor) and cautions not to send notice to addresses intended only for Solicitor mail service. A copy and fee must also be filed with the Federal Circuit clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of review by the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit applies 'substantial evidence' for review of fact findings and de novo review for questions of law; where legal conclusions are based on underlying facts the legal conclusion is reviewed without formal deference and subsidiary factual findings are reviewed for substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial evidence means such relevant evidence as a reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion; the court will review factual findings for this standard and will apply de novo review to legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following Federal Circuit decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit issues its mandate, the mandate is entered in the application/reexamination/interference file and the file is returned to the appropriate USPTO official for further proceedings consistent with the mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims remain rejected, proceedings are considered terminated as of mandate date. If some claims are allowed, the file is processed for issuance on allowed claims and any remaining formal matters are handled. Remand, reopening, and examiner actions must follow agency policy and may require written approval for reopening after court decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil suits under 35 U.S.C. 145 — new evidence and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In a 35 U.S.C. 145 civil action, the plaintiff may introduce evidence not previously presented to the USPTO, but will generally be precluded from presenting new issues unless a reason of justice is shown for failure to present the issue to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence unavailable to the parties but withheld from the USPTO due to fraud, bad faith, or gross negligence is not admissible. Copies of the complaint and summons must be served timely on the Solicitor, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, and the Attorney General pursuant to Rule 4(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers and Solicitor mail service address policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Court papers in which the Commissioner is a party must be served on the Solicitor of the Patent and Trademark Office by hand or mail to the specified Solicitor address. The Solicitor mail service address must not be used for filing notices of appeal to the Federal Circuit or for noncourt USPTO papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand service hours and mailing address are prescribed. Any noncourt papers mailed to the Solicitor mail service address will be returned to sender—no exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal or dismissal of appeal; partial withdrawal; claims standing allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP sets out procedures for withdrawal or dismissal of appeals, partial withdrawal, and treatment of claims that stand allowed when an appeal is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal may be withdrawn by appellant or dismissed for failure to prosecute; if any claims stand allowed, dismissal ordinarily will not cause abandonment and the examiner handles allowed claims for issuance or formal matters as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing and new grounds of rejection by the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may grant rehearings and may also enter new grounds of rejection in its decision, subject to procedural protections for appellant (e.g., opportunity to respond or remand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board enters a new ground of rejection, procedures govern publication, service, and the appellant's options (e.g., remand to examiner or request reopening of prosecution). See MPEP sections on Board's new grounds practice.
